_about: Colours for the LAC's meshes that take their colours from an atlas, keyed by the mesh names of our CAD export (lac.glb), in the form tools/build_model.py colour_from_atlas reads (bbox_min / bbox_max, solids {name, min, max, colour}; each solid's box in its part's own frame, mm). Two sources. (1) The Nano Board, which the LAC shares with the MRA: the MRA's entry for nano_Varsayılan, copied unchanged from colour-atlas-mra.json (the LAC's Nano is the MRA's export of the same model, nano-mra.glb). (2) Everything else from TechBox's own published LAC Cadasio project (instructions.online 19075-lac_full_build, docs/research/lac/cadasio/raw), read per solid as tools/cadasio/atlas.py does: each solid's colour is the one it is shown with most often. Single-colour meshes are under _single_colour. Written 19 Oct 2026 (first draft). Cadasio's coloured face copies (Surface-Offset: the resistors' bands, the knob's silver, the breadboard's printing, the Mini-B plug's and the switch's marks) are marked skin, so the face underneath takes their colour (as the LSM's atlas; Lee, 20 Oct 2026: the bands and the knob's ring showed the body through).

Piezo Buzzer._note: Stub colours from Cadasio's lying copy (Piezo Buzzer-1, published Steps 33 - 43: red stub and red lead to j4, as the captions say), not its clamped copy (Piezo Buzzer-2, which has them the other way round, its red lead going to (-) blue). The CAD wires solid [2] (seated x 674.5) to j4 in both poses. Lee, 21 Oct 2026: the stubs were the wrong colours against the leads (docs/research/lac/round2/buzzer_leads.md).
